stack: Static single-page app in plain JavaScript (ES modules) and HTML page fragments, built by build.mjs with esbuild into committed index.html, app.js, styles.css, cloud.js and words.json; word data in data/*.txt; Firebase (Google sign-in, Firestore, Firebase AI Logic with Gemini, optional App Check); Google Apps Script for the weekly e-mail and the Power BI export; node:test for checks; GitHub Pages from the main branch

idea.need: People who work in IT need one place to look up the IT words for their job and level, hear them, and find any word fast, in English or in their own language.
idea.intent: Learners in all nine IT roles (students, developers, testers, BA/PO/PM, PMO, IT HR, business development, sales, managers) get a searchable library of IT words at three levels, each with IPA, a definition, meanings in Vietnamese, Korean and French, a workplace example and audio. Partners such as BAPO Path can link straight to one role's words.
idea.problem: IT vocabulary is spread across courses and glossaries, is rarely sorted by role or level, and seldom comes with pronunciation and a meaning in the learner's language, so learners cannot quickly find and practise the words their job needs.
users: Content maintainer (edits data/ and runs the build)
idea.outcomeMetric: Done when every word in words.json has a term, part of speech, IPA, English definition, Vietnamese, Korean and French meanings, an example, a topic, a level from 1 to 3 and at least one known role; when a learner can find any word in Browse by typing it (or its meaning) in English, Vietnamese, Korean or French and narrow the list by level, role, topic and status; and when a ?role= link opens the site filtered to that role.
scopeIn: Word database built from data/*.txt by build.mjs, with definitions (data/definitions), French meanings (data/fr), IPA (CMU dictionary plus data/pronunciation-overrides.json), level overrides and role tagging (roles.mjs)
Abbreviation cards: an abbreviation and its full form merged into one card (data/merge-abbreviations.txt)
Role link (#<page>?role=<id>) and the focus bar with See the words and Show all roles
Browse search across term, full form, English definition, Vietnamese, Korean and French, ignoring accents
Browse filters: level, role, topic (business domains and IT topics), status (new, learning, known, saved)
Select mode and bulk actions: mark as learnt, still learning, save, remove from saved, reset to new
Listen buttons using the device's speech voices, with a slow button in the word dialog, accent and speed settings
scopeOut: Recorded human audio: all audio is the device's text-to-speech voice
Word photos: cards show topic icons only (photos were removed on 2026-11-01)
Bulk actions outside Browse (select mode closes when the learner leaves Browse)
risks: Speech voices depend on the device; some devices have no voice for a language or accent
Meanings and IPA come from data files and AI tools and may be wrong until a learner reports them
The ?role= parameter only works inside the hash (#home?role=ba); a link like /?role=ba is only counted as a visit source and does not filter. The README says ?role= works on "any page link".
A guest who clicks Save or a mark button must sign in first, which may put off casual visitors

A full form merged into an abbreviation is not checked for IPA: if its IPA cannot be worked out, the build still passes and the card shows no IPA for the full form (build.mjs:135 copies it before the missing-IPA check at :144). Today every merged full form has one.

Some level overrides have no effect: an override on an abbreviation is undone by the merge with its full form (data/level-overrides.txt has UAT|2, but UAT is level 1 because "user acceptance testing" is level 1).

A term repeated on a later line (in the same or a later data file) keeps the first line's part of speech, meaning, example, topic and level without a warning; only the roles are combined (build.mjs:85). For example, approve in data/2-dev.txt and reliability at data/6-extra-l3.txt:43 look edited but change nothing.

Home page text is out of date: it says "Every word has a picture" (words have topic icons only) and "Your progress is saved in this browser" (progress is saved only for signed-in learners) (src/pages/home.html:7, :47, :55).

Not checked in a browser: after a guest signs in from the bulk-action pop-up, the action runs again about 300 ms later, and loading the account then joins its saved, known and learning words with the local ones (src/ui-cloud.js:28-33, :321). If the account loads after the action, "Remove from saved" and "Reset to new" may be undone for words the account already had.
A data line with fewer than five fields is skipped: the build prints "BAD LINE" but still succeeds, so the term silently disappears (build.mjs:83).

idea.need: Learners in Vietnam and Korea, and French readers, should see meanings, translations and the site itself in their own language, and people without a tech background need words explained in everyday language.
idea.intent: Each learner chooses any of Vietnamese, Korean and French next to English and an interface language; meanings, example translations, plain explanations and stories then appear in those languages, with listen buttons for translated sentences. Non-technical roles see plain explanations on cards automatically.
idea.problem: A single translation language does not fit a mixed audience, an English-only interface is a barrier for beginners, and IT definitions are hard to follow for HR, sales and managers.
users: Non-technical learner (IT HR, business development, sales, managers)
Admin (runs the AI tools that write translations, explanations and stories)
idea.outcomeMetric: Done when a learner can choose any mix of Vietnamese, Korean and French and see meanings (and, where the word has them, example translations, plain explanations and stories) in each chosen language; can switch the interface to one of their languages or to English plus their languages; and when HR, business development, sales and manager learners see plain explanations on word cards without changing a setting.
scopeIn: Meaning languages Vietnamese, Korean, French (any combination) chosen in My profile or the globe button; English always shown
Interface language: English only, one chosen language only, or English plus my languages, from data/i18n.txt
Listen buttons in each language's voice for example translations and story translations
Plain-language explanations with an Automatic / Always show / Only in the word details setting
Stories for complex words in the word dialog
Preferences kept in the browser for guests and in the account for signed-in learners
scopeOut: Languages other than English, Vietnamese, Korean and French
Listen buttons for meanings and for plain explanations
Plain explanations, stories and example translations in the built-in words.json: they exist only after an admin runs the AI tools and they are read from Firestore
risks: Translations, explanations and stories are AI-written and may be wrong until checked or reported
If Firestore content has not been published or the AI tools have not run, no plain explanations, stories or example translations appear at all
Devices without a Vietnamese, Korean or French voice read translations with the wrong voice
Interface strings missing from data/i18n.txt stay in English

requirements.title: Word database with levels, roles, topics, IPA, meanings and examples
requirements.story: As a content maintainer I want the build to turn the data files into one checked word database so that every word card has complete, consistent data.
ac:
Given a term appears on one or more lines of the data/<digit>*.txt files (read in file-name order, then line order), each below a header such as "# level=2 role=dev"
When the maintainer runs npm run build
Then words.json has one word for the term: its part of speech, Vietnamese meaning, example and topic come from the term's first line, its starting level is the header level of that first line, and its starting roles are the header roles of every line it appears on

Given the first line in data/definitions (files in name order) that gives the term both an English definition and a Korean meaning is "term|English definition|Korean meaning"
When the maintainer runs npm run build
Then the word has that English definition (d) and Korean meaning (k); if no line gives the term both, the build prints "Missing definitions in data/definitions/:" with the term and exits non-zero

Given the first line in data/fr (files in name order, not corporate.txt) that gives the term a French meaning is "term|French meaning"
When the maintainer runs npm run build
Then the word has that French meaning (f); a word with no French line gets an empty one and the build only warns

Given a line "term|level" in data/level-overrides.txt
When the maintainer runs npm run build
Then that level replaces the word's starting level, before roles.mjs adds roles (next AC) and before abbreviations are merged; if the term is not a word or the level is not 1, 2 or 3, the build prints "data/level-overrides.txt: not found or bad level" with the line and exits non-zero

Given any word, with or without a line in data/level-overrides.txt
When the maintainer runs npm run build
Then after the level overrides, roles.mjs adds roles to the word using its term, topic, starting roles and its level after any override, and the word's roles are its starting roles plus the roles roles.mjs adds; abbreviations are merged after this

Given a line "ABBR|full form" in data/merge-abbreviations.txt, after level overrides and roles.mjs
When the maintainer runs npm run build
Then words.json keeps one card for ABBR whose full form (a) is the full form's term with its IPA (ai), whose level is the lower of the two words' levels, whose roles are those of both, and whose empty meanings and definition are filled from the full form; the full form's own card is removed, and the card shows "= <full form>" under the term with its own listen button; if either term is not a word, the build prints "data/merge-abbreviations.txt: not found" and exits non-zero

Given a kept word (not a full form merged into an abbreviation) whose IPA cannot be worked out from the dictionary or data/pronunciation-overrides.json
When the maintainer runs npm run build
Then the build prints "Add these to data/pronunciation-overrides.json first:" with the term and exits non-zero

requirements.title: Open the site for one role with a link
requirements.story: As a partner site (for example BAPO Path) I want to link learners to one role's words so that they see the vocabulary for their job straight away.
ac:
Given a visitor opens #home?role=ba
When the page loads
Then a bar shows "Showing words for BA / PO / PM · <n> of <total> words" with See the words and Show all roles, the Browse role filter, the flashcard role and the quiz role are set to BA / PO / PM, and the address becomes #home

Given a role was chosen by a link
When the visitor reloads the page in the same browser
Then the bar and the role filter are still set to that role

Given the role bar is showing
When the visitor clicks Show all roles, or opens a link with ?role=all
Then the bar disappears and Browse shows all roles

Given a first-time visitor with no role opens #home?role=ba
When the page loads
Then the first-visit role picker is not shown and My role is set to BA / PO / PM

requirements.title: Search and filter the word library
requirements.story: As a learner I want to search in English or my own language and filter by level, role, topic and status so that I find the words I need quickly.
ac:
Given the Browse page
When the learner types a word in the search box in English, Vietnamese (with or without accents), Korean or French
Then the grid shows words whose term, full form, English definition, Vietnamese, Korean or French meaning contains it, terms that start with it first, and the count shows "<n> words"

Given the Browse page
When the learner picks a level, a role, a topic (grouped under Business domains and IT topics, each with its word count) and a status (All words, New, Learning, Known, Saved ★)
Then only words matching all chosen filters are shown

Given a role filter and no search text
When the list is shown
Then words whose main role is that role come first, then by level

Given more than 36 matching words
When the list is shown
Then 36 cards appear with "Show more words (<n> left)", and each click shows 48 more

Given no word matches
When the list is shown
Then the message "No words match. Try another search or clear the filters." appears

requirements.title: Select many words and mark them at once
requirements.story: As a signed-in learner I want to select many words and mark, save or reset them together so that I do not have to open each card.
ac:
Given the Browse page
When the learner clicks Select words
Then cards become selectable, the button changes to Select all shown and a bar appears with "<n> selected", Mark as learnt, Still learning, Save, Remove from saved, Reset to new and Done

Given a signed-in learner has selected words
When they click Mark as learnt, Still learning, Save, Remove from saved or Reset to new
Then every selected word gets that status, a message such as "<n> words marked as learnt." shows, and Still learning schedules each word for a 1-day review

Given a guest has selected words
When they click a bulk action once the site knows they are not signed in
Then the "Save your progress with Google" pop-up opens and nothing is marked; after signing in from the pop-up the action is applied to the selection

Given select mode with no word selected
When the learner clicks a bulk action
Then the message "Select some words first." shows

Given select mode is on
When the learner clicks Done or leaves Browse
Then select mode ends and the selection is cleared

requirements.title: Listen to words and examples
requirements.story: As a learner I want to hear each word, its full form and its example so that I learn how to say them.
ac:
Given a word card, the word dialog, a flashcard or the word of the day
When the learner taps a listen button
Then the device reads the term (or the full form, or the example sentence) aloud in the English accent chosen in My profile (American or British) at the chosen speed

Given the word dialog
When the learner taps the slow listen button
Then the term is read at 0.6 speed

Given a browser without speech synthesis
When the learner taps a listen button
Then the message "Audio is not supported in this browser. Use the IPA to check the sound." shows

requirements.title: Choose meaning languages
requirements.story: As a learner I want to choose which of Vietnamese, Korean and French appear next to English so that I see meanings in the languages I read.
ac:
Given a new visitor
When they open a word card
Then the English definition is shown with the Vietnamese and Korean meanings (the default languages), Vietnamese in bold as the first language

Given My profile → Languages, or the globe button in the top bar
When the learner ticks or unticks Tiếng Việt, 한국어 or Français
Then word cards, the word dialog and flashcards show the English definition plus a meaning row for each ticked language, and the globe button shows the chosen languages (for example "VI·FR") or "EN" when none is ticked

Given the learner's first chosen language is Korean
When they get a "What does this word mean?" quiz question or take the level test
Then the answer options show the Korean meanings, falling back to the English definition where a word has none

Given a guest changes languages
When they reload the page in the same browser
Then the same languages are chosen, and the Languages card says "Saved in this browser. Sign in to use them on every device."

Given a signed-in learner changes languages on one device
When they sign in on another device
Then the most recently changed preferences are used

requirements.title: Choose the interface language
requirements.story: As a learner who is new to English I want the menus and buttons in my language so that I can use the site without getting lost.
ac:
Given the learner has chosen Vietnamese and French as meaning languages
When they open Website interface
Then the options are English only, Tiếng Việt only, Français only and English + my languages

Given the learner picks Tiếng Việt only
When any page is shown
Then interface text listed in data/i18n.txt is shown in Vietnamese, while words, meanings, examples and names stay as they are

Given the learner picks English + my languages
When any page is shown
Then each translated interface text shows the English followed by its translation in each chosen language

Given the interface is in French
When the learner unticks Français as a meaning language
Then the interface switches to English only

Given a line in data/i18n.txt without exactly four parts separated by " | "
When the maintainer runs npm run build
Then the build exits non-zero naming the line

requirements.title: Listen to translations in their own language
requirements.story: As a learner I want to hear example and story translations in that language's voice so that I can check my understanding by ear.
ac:
Given a word whose example has translations and the learner has chosen Korean
When they tap the listen button on the Korean example row
Then the translation is read with a Korean (ko-KR) voice; Vietnamese uses vi-VN and French fr-FR

Given the device has speech voices, but none for the chosen language
When the learner taps that language's listen button
Then the message "No <language> voice on this device, so it may sound wrong. Add one in your system settings." shows

Given a word dialog with a story
When the learner opens the story in a chosen language
Then that translation has its own listen button in that language's voice

requirements.title: Plain-language explanations
requirements.story: As a learner without a tech background (HR, business development, sales or a manager) I want each word explained in everyday language so that I understand what my IT colleagues mean.
ac:
Given the plain-language setting is Automatic (the default) and My role is IT HR, Business development, Sales or Manager / C-level
When the learner sees a word card in Browse, Saved words or the word of the day for a word that has a plain explanation
Then the card shows "In plain words" with the English explanation, and the back of the flashcard shows it in English and each chosen language

Given the setting is Automatic and My role is Developers, Testers, BA / PO / PM, PMO, University students or not set
When the learner sees a word card
Then no plain explanation is shown on the card

Given the setting is Always show
When any learner sees a word card or the back of a flashcard for a word that has a plain explanation
Then the explanation is shown (on the flashcard also in each chosen language)

Given any setting, including Only in the word details
When the learner opens the word dialog for a word that has a plain explanation
Then "In plain words" is shown in English and in each chosen language

requirements.title: Stories for complex words
requirements.story: As a learner I want a short real-life story for hard words so that I see how the word is used at work.
ac:
Given a word that has a story
When the learner opens its word dialog
Then "Story: how it works in real life" shows the English story with a listen button, and each chosen language as a collapsible section named after the language

Given a word without a story
When the learner opens its word dialog
Then no story section is shown

Given an admin runs the AI tool Stories for complex words
When it picks words
Then it only writes stories for level 3 words, level 2 words in the architecture, cloud, security, data, AI, Agile, release, process, performance, network, business or money topics, and multi-word terms at level 2 or 3

decisions.title: Static site on GitHub Pages with the build output committed to main
decisions.context: Decided before Compass was adopted; recorded when the project was onboarded to the Compass Framework (2026-11-27). Back-filled from the README and git history; confirmed by the Product Owner on 2026-11-27.
decisions.decision: build.mjs generates index.html, app.js, styles.css, cloud.js and words.json from src/ and data/, and those files are committed. GitHub Pages serves the main branch as it is, with no deploy workflow.
decisions.consequences: Every change to src/ or data/ must be rebuilt (npm run build) and the generated files committed in the same PR; Compass CI fails when they are stale. The Compass deploy workflow (compass-deploy.yml) is not installed.

decisions.title: Firebase on the free plan: Google sign-in and Firestore, content read as packed bundles
decisions.context: Decided before Compass was adopted; recorded when the project was onboarded to the Compass Framework (2026-11-27). Back-filled from the README and git history; confirmed by the Product Owner on 2026-11-27.
decisions.decision: Learner accounts, progress, lists, reports and the word content live in Firestore. The site reads words as packed bundles of 150 words (bundles/words-01…), so a visit costs about 20 reads. Access is controlled by firestore.rules; admins are listed in admins/{uid}.
decisions.consequences: Changes to firestore.rules change who can read and write data, so the file is a protected path. Built-in words reach Firestore only when an admin runs Admin → Content & sync → Sync.

decisions.title: AI features run in the browser through Firebase AI Logic (Gemini) on the free tier
decisions.context: Decided before Compass was adopted; recorded when the project was onboarded to the Compass Framework (2026-11-27). Back-filled from the README and git history; confirmed by the Product Owner on 2026-11-27.
decisions.decision: Translations, plain explanations, stories and My lists extraction call Gemini through Firebase AI Logic, trying several flash models in turn (src/cloud.js TEXT_MODELS), with long timeouts for slow free-tier replies. App Check protects the AI quota when a site key is set in src/firebase-config.js.
decisions.consequences: No server or API key to manage. AI output must be checked by a person; learners report mistakes and admins fix them.

decisions.title: Word ids stay stable: new word files are added at the end
decisions.context: Decided before Compass was adopted; recorded when the project was onboarded to the Compass Framework (2026-11-27). Back-filled from the README and git history; confirmed by the Product Owner on 2026-11-27.
decisions.decision: Word ids are assigned in the order of the data/ files, so new files are added at the end (e.g. 10-…txt) and existing lines are not reordered.
decisions.consequences: Progress, lists and reports refer to word ids; reordering data files would point them at the wrong words.

decisions.title: Insights and visit counts store no names or e-mails
decisions.context: Decided before Compass was adopted; recorded when the project was onboarded to the Compass Framework (2026-11-27). Back-filled from the README and git history; confirmed by the Product Owner on 2026-11-27.
decisions.decision: Admin → Insights counts signed-in learners only and stores no names or e-mails; visits/{date} holds anonymous daily counts; the Power BI export shows learners only as an anonymous code.
decisions.consequences: Personal data stays out of analytics; any new metric must keep to this rule.

decisions.title: The public Firebase web API key is allowed by the secret scan
decisions.context: Decided before Compass was adopted; recorded when the project was onboarded to the Compass Framework (2026-11-27). Back-filled from the README and git history; confirmed by the Product Owner on 2026-11-27.
decisions.decision: compass/guardrails.json keeps the Google API key pattern (AIza…) but exempts this project's own Firebase web API key, which is public by design (src/firebase-config.js) and bundled into cloud.js on one long line.
decisions.consequences: Without the exemption, every rebuild of cloud.js would fail the guardrails check. Any other Google API key is still blocked.

decisions.title: GitHub Pages serves the site without Jekyll
decisions.context: The site is prebuilt by build.mjs (ADR-001), but GitHub Pages still ran Jekyll on the main branch. Jekyll renders Markdown files without front matter, so Liquid tags (double curly braces, or a brace followed by a percent sign) in any compass/*.md would fail the Pages build and stop the live site from updating. Raised in the independent review of #2; the Product Owner asked for the fix.
decisions.decision: An empty .nojekyll at the repository root turns Jekyll off; Pages serves the committed files as they are.
decisions.consequences: Markdown files are no longer turned into HTML pages on the site (none are linked from it). Files and folders starting with _ or . (such as .github/, .claude/settings.json and .gitignore) are served too; none holds a secret, and the repo is public.

decisions.title: Back-fill the shipped features as Done requirements, two features per PR
decisions.context: The ten features built before Compass was adopted were not in the spec. Writing them up touches about 36 files, and the guardrails cap a PR at 12 files (the human-approved label does not lift that cap). The Product Owner chose to keep the cap and split the work, to number the back-fill in its own blocks (ADR-101, REQ-101, TC-101) so it stays clear of the ids that other open work uses, and to give every acceptance criterion its own test case.
decisions.decision: Each shipped feature becomes F-001…F-010, with requirements REQ-101 onwards written from what the code does today (status Done, sources listing the code). Every acceptance criterion gets its own test case, and the concrete example scenarios are kept as extra test cases. They go in five PRs of two features each. Test cases are Manual with status Not run unless an automated test covers them. Features get no design object: they predate the design stage.
decisions.consequences: Every acceptance criterion is traced to a test case, but most tests have not been run yet; QA can run them and set Pass or Fail. New ADRs, requirements and test cases take the next free id below the back-fill blocks, after checking main and every open branch. Gaps found while writing (README drift, possible bugs) are listed as risks on the feature, not fixed in these PRs.
